content_html:
Frontend development services: React, Next.js, Vue and more

Frontend development builds everything visitors see and use in the browser: layouts, menus, forms and interactive features. Modern frontend work uses frameworks like React, Next.js, Angular and Vue. React has the largest ecosystem, Angular suits large structured teams, Vue is light and easy to learn, and Next.js adds the SEO and speed features business websites need.

What does frontend development cover?

The frontend is the part of a website that runs in the visitor's browser. It turns designs into responsive pages, handles clicks and forms, loads data from the back end and keeps the site fast and accessible. Good frontend work directly affects Core Web Vitals, conversions and how easily search engines read your pages.

React vs Angular vs Vue: which frontend framework is best?

ReactAngularVue
TypeUI libraryFull frameworkProgressive framework
StrengthLargest ecosystem and talent poolStructure for big enterprise teamsLightweight and easy to learn
Learning curveModerateSteeperGentle
Good forMost web apps and sitesLarge, complex business appsSmall to mid-size apps, quick builds

There is no single best framework. Choose based on your team's skills, the project's size, your SEO needs and who will maintain it later.

Next.js vs React

React builds user interfaces. Next.js is a framework built on React that adds routing, server-side rendering, static generation and image optimisation. For public websites that must rank and load fast, Next.js is usually the better choice. Plain React suits internal tools and dashboards. Read how rendering affects rankings in website SEO and performance.

Other frontend tools worth knowing

  • TypeScript adds types to JavaScript. It catches errors early and makes large codebases easier to maintain.
  • Tailwind CSS is utility-first and great for custom design systems. Bootstrap offers ready components for faster standard layouts.
  • Svelte produces very small bundles and simple code, with a smaller ecosystem than React.

How to choose a frontend stack

  1. Is the site public and SEO-critical? Prefer Next.js or another framework with server rendering.
  2. Is it a large enterprise app with many developers? Consider Angular or React with TypeScript.
  3. Do you need to ship quickly with a small team? Vue or Next.js are strong options.
  4. Can you hire for it locally? Check the talent pool before you commit.

Frontend development at Openink Hub

What good frontend development looks like in practice

First, good frontend development starts on the smallest screen and then scales up. Next, it keeps pages light. For example, it compresses images, loads scripts only when needed and avoids heavy sliders. In addition, it follows accessibility rules, so buttons, forms and menus work with a keyboard and a screen reader. Then it measures results with Core Web Vitals and fixes the slowest pages first. Also, it connects cleanly to your CMS, whether WordPress or a headless system, so editors can update content without breaking layouts. As a result, visitors get fast, clear pages, and search engines get pages they can crawl and understand. Finally, a good frontend team documents its components, so future changes stay quick and consistent.

We build fast, accessible, SEO-ready frontends and connect them to the right back end. See every technology we work with on our technology services page, explore our website development services, or talk to us.

Frequently asked questions

React vs Angular vs Vue: which is best?

None is best for everyone. React has the biggest ecosystem, Angular suits large structured teams, and Vue is light and easy to learn.

Which frontend framework is best for SEO?

Frameworks that render pages on the server or at build time, such as Next.js or Nuxt, are best for SEO-critical public websites.

What is the difference between Next.js and React?

React is a library for building interfaces. Next.js is a framework built on React that adds routing, server rendering and performance features.

Which framework is easiest to learn?

Vue is usually the easiest to start with; React is moderate; Angular has the steepest learning curve.

What are common framework selection mistakes?

Choosing for hype instead of team skills, ignoring SEO needs, and picking a stack nobody in your market can maintain.
